study_identification_part.si4_title: Closing the life-cycle of normative modeling using federated hierarchical Bayesian regression

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Proposes a federated hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) framework to complete the life-cycle of normative modeling on decentralized multi-site neuroimaging data, handling site effects, enabling parameter updating/extension, and model adaptation for local clinical deployment.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: ABCD; CamCAN; CMI; CNP; FCON; HCP; HCPAG; HCPDV; HCPEP; IXI; NKI; OASIS3; OPN; PNC; TOP; UKBB
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper explicitly lists all 16 datasets used in Table 1, with full names and abbreviations. These datasets include healthy controls and clinical populations across 79 scanners.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Table 1 lists the 16 neuroimaging datasets that are used in our experiments. For the ABCD dataset [15], we used data from the first imaging timepoint for subjects included in the v 2.0.1 curated release. For the UK Biobank (UKBB) study [10], we used approximately 15000 subjects derived from the 2017 release. For the Human Connectome Project aging, development and early psychosis studies (HCPAG, HCPDV and HCPEP, respectively) we used data from the 1.0 data release.
rci1_dataset_name.location: Kia2022.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Datasets and preprocessing, L204-205, and Table 1 L218-237

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: HBR provides accurate normative ranges and mitigates site-effects relative to naive pooling and ComBat-based pooling; supports federated estimation, sequential extension, and parameter transfer for local adaptation; deviations quantified via z-scores/Pabn show disease-related abnormalities across regions.
